title: 1801 Prairie's upper windows raised and its 18th Street arched pair
items: W. W. Kimball's house at 1801 Prairie: the upper-floor windows now stand taller, their heads raised about 0.3 m under the stone cornice, each with a transom light across its top, as J. W. Taylor's c. 1895 photograph shows them.

On the 18th Street side, between the round tower and the corner, the single window on each floor is now a pair of round-headed lights upstairs over plain stone below, as in the photograph; the corner window over the arch moves a little east to where the photograph has it.
